sections.text: I am the Thunderbolt among weapons; of cows I am the Cow of Plenty, I am Passion in those who procreate, and I am the Cobra among serpents.
I am the King-python among snakes, I am the Aqueous Principle among those that live in water, I am the Father of fathers, and among rulers I am Death.
And I am the devotee Prahlad among the heathen; of Time I am the Eternal Present; I am the Lion among beasts and the Eagle among birds.

We have been discussing Chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, Yoga of Divine Glories. Bhagavan, in the beginning of the chapter, made two basic points. First: all these divine qualities which you see in beings , such as Buddhi, jnana, Asamoha, Samata, Ahimsa, Dana, Bhaya, Abhaya , all these qualities emanate from me.
Because of my presence in them, they manifest these qualities. So whenever you see these qualities, know that I am present in that being. And then he said: Aham Sarvasya Prabhavah, Mattaha Sarva Pravartate.
There is nothing that is not based in me. I am the source of all things and beings, and everything proceeds from me. So Bhagawan has made it very clear that there is nothing which is devoid of him.
But Arjuna obviously wanted examples in his world which he can relate to. So thats what he said: Keshu Keshu Bhaveshu Chintyo Asi Bhagavan maya. In what different forms that I see in this world can I worship as your presence? If I have to find examples of divinity which are worthy of worship, tell me , how do I find them, how do I recognize them, and how do I approach them? Therefore, Bhagavan said: when you see anything which is best among that category, consider that worthy of worshipping.
Excellence is worthy of worshipping. Yogah Karmasu Kaushalam , proficiency is worshipable. Anything which is efficient and proficient.
Bhagawan said, consider that is my manifestation. It is worthy of worship. So therefore, Bhagavan has been giving various examples of best among those categories.
And we have seen so far Bhagawan started with Vedic examples based rooted in the culture of Vedic period. And then he has given some examples which are common between Vedic and Puranic period. And then he has been giving examples from Puranic period.
In other words, hes covering all that Arjuna has experienced, ancestral, past, folklore. And then Also the day to day world where Im trying to find divinity. I try to find divinity in my great culture.
Also try to find divinity in the folklore which Ive heard from people. And I also try to find divinity in my world. Verses 27, 28, 29 continues in that tradition.
We are seeing more Puranic examples. Ucchaihshravasam Ashvanam Viddhi Mam Amritod Bhavam , among the horses, Ucchaihshravas, which came out of the endeavor of finding nectar. It is the story of churning the milky ocean to find the nectar of immortality.
But byproducts of that effort we can call Riddhi and Siddhi. This churning of the ocean is nothing but churning your own mind. One side is bad and other side is good thoughts.
Bad thoughts and good thoughts are churning your mind. What comes out of it are the byproducts I call Riddhi and Siddhi. When we try to achieve the final goal of liberation or immortality or ultimate happiness, whichever you want to call it, we are constantly churning our mind to find that ultimate happiness.
In that process we achieve some accomplishments. Those are Siddhi and Riddhi. We get these along our pursuit of happiness.
We have not got the happiness yet, but we get some things which are byproducts of the pursuit. So me buying a BMW, or Albany and Maulik going to Hawaii , you people went to Hawaii and I bought a BMW X5 Hybrid over the weekend. So we covered two bases of my Vedantic journey.
Now you have to go to Starbucks to complete the third leg of it. All that is in pursuit of happiness. Thats why I want to go to Hawaii.
Thats why I want to buy BMW. But that is not the end goal. Bhagavan says the end goal is to find the nectar.
The nectar is endless happiness without any break in it. That is what we call immortality. That is also what we call liberation.
So this churning of the ocean , Viddhi Mam Amritod Bhavam. This flying horse came out of the pursuit of happiness as an excellent achievement from the pursuit of finding something else. They were not looking for a flying horse; they were looking for nectar.
But what came out? A flying horse , the best among the horses. We become excellent in our profession. That actually was the goal.
I want to make more money. Then I became very proficient in my profession. We consider unfortunately that is the goal.
That never was my goal. My goal was to be happy. But I sometimes become so Enamored by my own achievement that I just stop right there, that Im the best.
So Bhagavan said, among horses, Uche Shravaha, the flying horse which came out of the journey of ocean, Airavatam, Gajendrana both came out of the same pursuit. The white elephant with many tusks came out. Airavat and Cheshrava, the flying horse came.
They both came in same pursuit of finding nectar. The airavat was given to Indra, but horse was given to Daitya. But both came out as excellent examples of something you can accomplish by your pursuit of finding nectar.
Bliss Naranamcha, Naradhipah among men. I am the king among man. When somebody becomes as powerful as one can be, he is called king.
Airavat is an example among elephants, Uchesa among horses. So in all living beings you find example of excellence. In our culture the king is considered divine representation.
Not only in our culture, but all Western cultures also King was considered divine. He is the one who is supporting the whole kingdom by his own action. Therefore he is considered divine.
Anything that is excellent among man, among animals, among beings of any kind considered to be my manifestation is worthy of worshipping. Because the original question was Keshu, Keshu, Chabhesu. So Bhagavan is giving him various examples.
Ayudhanam Aham Vajraha. Not only beings but things. Among the weapons and Vajra.
Vajra was conceived by Indra as the weapon which can kill the demon Vritrasur. He was the snake in a human form. The snake is generally considered poisonous.
So something which is poisonous and in stopping my progress bad thoughts in my mind. So Vhtrasu is my negative tendencies. And to kill that I need a weapon which is powerful and effective.
So here Indra to kill Vritrasur wanted Vajra, the ultimate weapon to kill this demon who was stopping the course of rivers. So he was someone who was stopping the progress. So Vritrasur can be only be killed by something which is very pious and self sacrificing.
So Indra found the Dhiji is the right candidate. He has all the positive qualities selfless in his endeavors. And when the Dichi approached, he agreed to give up his body.
And then his bones were used to make this Vajra. The meaning of this metaphor is if you have to kill the negative tendencies of your mind, you have to sacrifice. Selfless sacrifice is the only sure weapon to kill the negativity in your mind.
Of all the weapons to kill your negativity Bhagwan said, I am Vajra Denunam Asmi Kamaduk among cows. The milch cow was also described in chapter three in verse 10 where Bhagavan said Sahayagna prajasrustva Purvacha Prajapati Anena Prasi vistadvam ishacha asthu isht Kama dhak. In the beginning Prajapati said, I have created Praja in the same time Yajna.
This Yajna will be your Kamadhenu. This Yajna will be your cow which fulfills all your desires. So the Kamadenu is something which has capacity to fulfill all your desires.
And as for Purana, Vasisthta had this Kamadhina. Vasistha had this cow. This cow which can give whatever you desire like a genie in other Arabic tale.
Whatever you desire, genie can present. Bhagavan said, kamadhanu is your cooperative endeavors Yajna spirit. When you work together, when you combine your resources of your community, of your family, of your country then you can get whatever you want.
Dhienuna masmikamadu. In our culture cow is sacred because cow supports life. In olden days cow provided everything.
Cow provided milk for sustaining bodies. Cow also provided bullocks to till the land. Cow also provided cow dung for source of fuel.
That cow dung was also his building material to plaster the floors. The cow has ultimate giving capacity that it can sustain life. And and therefore cow is considered sacred.
But among all cows Bhagavan said, I am Kama Dhuk. I am Kama Dhenu which has capacity to fulfill all desires. And as Bhagawana said in chapter three, Kama Denu is your Yajna spirit.
When you work selflessly and work together you can fulfill all your desires. Prajanastya Asmi Kandarpah among the progenitor. I am that instinct to create progeny.
This instinct, Bhagavan said, is divine. Normally any sexual instinct we consider it to be negative, not good. Our culture clearly says thats divine.
Anything which is natural has to be divine. So this instinct to further your progeny is a divine instinct. Attraction for the opposite sex is put in beings by Bhagavan for a reason and therefore it is divine.
If you dont get attracted by opposite sex, go and see a doctor. Theres something wrong with you. That is something natural and divine.
It is how you use it, how you Manage it makes it either divine or devilish. Prajanas chasmi Kandarpaha. Kandarpah is that innate attraction for the opposite sex in you.
I am that Sarpanam Asmi Vasukihi. We have discussed two types of snakes, Sarpa and naga. Sarpa is the unhooded snake.
Hooded snake is Naga. Snakes like pythons and other garden snakes. And they are not many times poisonous.
Python can kill you, but its not poisonous. Theres a Naga Panchami day at least in Surat where I grew up. All these guys will bring cobra in in their little basket.
And my mother will offer milk and give some donation. Naga cobra is poisonous. But Bhagavan said even that poisonous instinct in beings is also divine.
Because there is no other source for this poisonous instinct than God alone. Everything in this world, even though it seems negative from our perspective. When you change the perspective it becomes natural and necessary.
I very recently read an article I think in New York Times. Forest fires are necessary for the survival of the forest. Now that was complete revelation to me.
Because every time I see forest fire in California on the TV I say why cant they do something? Can they not figure out how to stop this thing? Or what is the purpose of this? And it really opened my eyes. That article said without forest fire, forest cannot survive because the undergrowth will be so dense the trees wont survive. The forest fires clean up the forest every year now, obviously out of control.
Anything creates disasters. And most of the forest fires are man made or man created. They are not naturally created.
So anything which I see negative may have been over manipulated by someone. But the actual phenomenon, whether it seems negative or positive, my perspective is natural and divine. So therefore you say Sarpanam Asmi Vasukihi.
Among serpents and Vasuki Vasukhi is the smallest snake on Shivas finger. Also used as the rope in churning the ocean. And Vasuki also selflessly volunteered to become that rope which are on the ocean among snakes.
And Vasuki who gives his services selflessly for the common good. Anantahacha Asminagana. And among Nagam Ananta Ananta endless.
Another name of Ananta Nageshanahaya. We have seen Vishnu lying on the sheshanag in a slumber. Lakshmi Ji massaging his feet and Lotus coming out of his navel and Brahmaji sitting on it.
So this thousand hooded snake is nothing but my mind. It is thousand different desires in thousand different directions. With that capacity when it is associated with Tamas and Rajas, it has creative urge.

These verses present perhaps the most challenging of Krishnas identifications: Prajanah cha asmi Kandarpah - I am the creative desire in beings (Kandarpa/Kama). The procreative instinct, often seen as unspiritual or base, is here declared divine. Anything natural, placed in beings for a purpose, partakes of divinity. The issue is never the instinct itself but how it is expressed - controlled or compulsive, sacred or profane. Similarly, Krishna is Vajra among weapons - the thunderbolt that destroys negativity - and Kamadhenu among cows - the wish-fulfilling power of cooperative endeavor (Yajna).
Even more striking: Sarpanam asmi Vasuki - among serpents, I am Vasuki, who selflessly served as the churning rope when gods and demons sought nectar. And among the hooded serpents (Nagas), I am Ananta (the endless one) upon whom Vishnu rests. The serpent represents the mind with its thousand desires moving in every direction; when this same energy supports the divine (as Ananta supports Vishnu), it becomes sacred. What seems dangerous becomes the very vehicle of the divine.
Today, contemplate the divinization of natural instincts. That drive you feel - for creation, for union, for achievement - is not inherently unspiritual. The question is: does it serve the whole or only the ego? Vasuki volunteered for service and was honored; Ananta supports the divine in rest. Can your desires become like Vasuki - offered in service? Like Ananta - supporting divine presence rather than chasing endless wants? Ask: What instincts do I judge as unspiritual? Can I see them instead as divine energy awaiting proper direction?
